shortDescription: By Nqobile DludlaSouth African retailer Shoprite Holdings JSE:SHP said on Tuesday its annual headline earnings rose by 12.2%, supported by steady sales growth and expansion in its core grocery business.The country's largest supermarket group said headline earnings per share from continuing operatio…

children: said on Tuesday its annual headline earnings rose by 12.2%, supported by steady sales growth and expansion in its core grocery business.

The country's largest supermarket group said headline earnings per share from continuing operations rose to 15.32 rand  ($0.95) in the 52 weeks ended June 28 from a restated 13.65 rand a year earlier.
Here are the rest of the results:
The group's earnings before interest, income tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased by 7.7% to 25.8 billion rand ($1.60 billion) from a restated 23.9 billion.
Sales increased 7.2% to 270.8 billion rand, with the core South Africa supermarkets segment increasing sales by 7.1% to 228.7 billion rand.
The rest of Africa supermarkets delivered 11% sales growth, with constant currency sales growth measuring 7.1%.
The board declared a final dividend of 566 cents per share, up 14.1%.
